messages:
maya: Quick results from the multi-tenant cohort scheduling run — wanted to share numbers and get opinions on fairness knobs. Ran 4 cohorts (prod-web, search, composer, trials) across two regions (us-west, eu-central) on A100 / H100 mixes.
noah: Nice. What were the config priors? batch_window and max_batch_tokens?
maya: Default scheduler with continuous-batcher + tilt fairness. We swept batch_window = [5ms, 20ms, 50ms] and max_batch_tokens = [256, 1024, 2048]. Also toggled kernel: flash_attn vs triton_mha.
elaine: Did you keep prefix caching enabled? That can skew throughput for search/cohort with long histories.
maya: Yes, prefix/KV cache on. Cohort traces were replayed from production logs (sampled).
samir: TL;DR numbers?
maya: Summary:
- H100 pool (50% capacity): best P95 latency for small batch_window=5ms but throughput drops for high concurrency cohorts.
- A100 pool: higher steady throughput at batch_window=20ms, max_batch_tokens=1024.
- Fairness: with tilt fairness disabled, trials cohort starves at peak (throughput -40%). Enabling tilt fairness at alpha=0.6 recovered trial throughput to -8% while sacrificing ~4% total throughput.
noah: Any kernel differences?
maya: Flash_attn reduced token latency ~12% on H100 for long sequences (~1k tokens) but caused increased variance for short-chat workloads. Triton_mha had steadier P99 across cohorts.
elaine: What about long-tail p99 under the tight window (5ms)?
maya: P99 spike observed for composer cohort with many short requests when batch_window=5ms and max_batch_tokens=256 — microburst coalescing wasn't effective. Increasing max_batch_tokens to 1024 smoothed out P99 but increased median by ~6ms.
samir: Did you try dynamic windowing (adaptive increase under load)?
maya: Yes, quick experiment: window_adaptive: true, target_latency_ms: 30. It kept P95 within target and improved fairness, but control loop oscillates if autoscale jitter present. Need smoothing on metric (EWMA 30s).
noah: Any quality regressions from quantization or kernel changes?
maya: Ran int8 quant for a subset (quant-recipe-2026-02). ROUGE/bleu style checks on eval prompts showed ~0.6% drop in task accuracy for composer, negligible for chat-style. We flagged it but it's acceptable for many cohorts.
elaine: Where are detailed CSVs/plots?
maya: perf-bot: upload s3 link?
perf-bot: New artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/multi-tenant/1862456789/results.csv and s3://redwood-bench/multi-tenant/1862456789/plots.zip. Also dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/dash/multi-tenant/1862456789
samir: Can you paste the scheduler snippet you used?
maya: Sure:
```yaml
scheduler:
  type: continuous-batcher
  batch_window_ms: 20
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  fairness:
    strategy: tilt
    alpha: 0.6
  adaptive_window:
    enabled: true
    target_latency_ms: 30
    ewma_alpha: 0.05
  kernel_preference: [flash_attn, triton_mha]
```
noah: Good. My take: use adaptive window + tilt fairness alpha=0.5-0.7 for mixed workloads. Prefer H100+flash_attn for long sequences, fall back to triton for short-chat heavy instances.
elaine: For prod rollout, we should A/B canary: 10% of traffic with new config and monitor p99 and per-cohort SLOs for 30m. If any cohort drops >10% throughput or p99 increases >25%, rollback.
maya: Agreed — will schedule canary for tonight. I'll attach canary playbook and the eval prompt set.
samir: One more ask: add a metric for "cohort fairness ratio" (min cohort throughput / median cohort throughput) so we can graph regressions over rollouts.
maya: Done — added to dashboard. I'll post a short follow-up after the canary. :thumbsup:
